milestones.21: Strict predictable kernels and costly-copy diagnostics
milestones.23: Composable effect contracts and callback rows
milestones.24: Scoped storage and deterministic resource ownership
milestones.26: Tensor shapes and explicit IEEE policy
milestones.28: Affine quantities and language-native test contracts
milestones.31: Flagship: durable key-value store and query layer
milestones.33: Web services with a wasm UI
milestones.35: Flagship: freestanding kernel in the strict lane
milestones.40: Fixed-width overflow policies and exact intermediates
milestones.59: Generic game boards sized by integer type arguments

64_strict_audio.note: 64 allocation-free fixed-buffer audio blocks; no hidden copy, detach or panic in the kernel.

65_reject_hidden_allocation.note: Reject dynamic allocation behind a no allocates signature.

66_reject_implicit_copy.note: Reject an implicit independent runtime-sized mutable copy.

expect.diagnostic: explicit cop|implicit cop|runtime-sized cop|implicit costly copy

67_reject_unproved_index.note: Reject indexing with unknown bounds rather than insert a panic (`$runtime_checks=false` until no traps is the default).

68_positive_divisors.note: Prove positive divisors and nonempty indexing through helpers and guards.

69_dependent_append.note: Carry returned index evidence across a mutable append and a search result.

70_reject_stale_fact.note: Reject stale index evidence after a length-changing place mutation (`$runtime_checks=false` until no traps is the default).

71_checked_proofs.note: Check and erase proof calls; retain transitive result facts at callers.

72_prototype_boundary.note: Prototype-deferred bounds become explicit runtime checks; checked code exports success facts.

73_place_effects.note: Translate reads/writes on place parameters through swapped arguments and sibling fields.

74_callback_rows.note: Forward nonlocal callback rows while remapping explicit place permissions.

75_reject_effect_violation.note: Reject a transitive external mutation inside no_effects.

76_arena_escape.note: Copies escaping nested allocator scopes survive reset and preserve independent aggregates.

77_owner_cleanup.note: Move last-use owners and release actual resources exactly once on return, break and continue; do not assert elidable copy-hook counts.

78_reject_resource_copy.note: Reject copying a drop-only owner while its original remains live.

79_scoped_byte_loan.note: Read scoped bytes, reserve and commit writable bytes, preserve snapshots after detach.

80_reject_loan_escape.note: Reject a raw address returned from a scoped storage loan.

81_partition_join.note: Fork owned disjoint partitions, join in source order, and prove coverage including an uneven tail.

82_overlap_race.note: Compile-time reject concurrent writes to overlapping ranges; accept adjacent partitions.

83_transfer_properties.note: Derive structural task-transfer properties; reject an Rc-like non-atomic handle crossing tasks.

84_tensor_broadcast.note: Contiguous rank-2 arrays, row/column broadcast, transpose, snapshot rows, and reject mismatched shapes.

85_ieee_policy.note: IEEE signed zero, subnormal, overflow/underflow, NaN comparisons and deterministic reduction under an explicit policy.

86_exact_energy.note: Exact irregular energy integration, decimal tariffs, split invariance and denominator growth.

87_big_arithmetic.note: Runtime bigint modular exponentiation, 100!, binomial exact division and big rational intermediates; arithmetic only, no cryptographic security claim.

88_temperature_points.note: Temperature point-minus-point and point-plus-delta, exact C/F/K conversions and requested display units.

89_test_contracts.note: Discover 10 case-expanded tests, report one failed helper expectation, continue the test and retain ordinary main.

90_stack_repl.note: Interactive stdin RPN interpreter: variables, arithmetic, rollback on parse/stack/divisor errors, EOF and quit; bounded integer parser.

91_adventure_state.note: Command-driven adventure with inventory, locked transitions, score, win state and copied save states.

92_http_json_routes.note: HTTP/1.1 request parser and JSON integer-schema CRUD routing with status codes and transactional validation; deterministic transport transcripts over a loopback listener.

93_table_queries.note: SQLite-like in-memory table, parsed insert/update/delete/select, primary keys, ordered queries and begin/commit/rollback; independent SQLite oracle.

94_physics_hash.note: 80 integer-step 2D physics frames, spatial hash broad phase cross-checked against all pairs, deterministic axis impulses, walls, conserved kinetic sum and saved world.

95_kv_store.note: Durable ordered key-value store in modules: B+ tree index, checksummed write-ahead log with atomic multi-key transactions, recovery of torn and damaged tails, two-slot manifest, crash-safe compaction, SQL subset with a key-range planner; SQLite-checked session and a seeded crash-injection workload against a model.

96_ct_crypto.note: SHA-256/HMAC/HKDF, ChaCha20, Poly1305, (X)ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519 and a replay-protected channel in modules, written without secret-dependent branches or indexing; FIPS 180-4, RFC 4231/5869/8439/7748 and XChaCha vectors, forgery and replay rejection, key-agreement-plus-AEAD workload. Constant time is not compiler-checked.

97_notes_service.note: Notes web service and UI (tier-4 flagship): HTTP/1.1 byte framing with limits, chunked bodies and pipelining; JSON CRUD with validation, revisions, conditional requests, atomic batches and static files; a UI state machine over the same wire bytes. Also runs as wasm (tests/test_flagship_web.py).

98_notes_listen.note: The notes service of 97 behind a real loopback listener (accept, partial reads, pipelining, close, EOF) plus the wasm page shell (ui_app.dewy, built by tests/test_flagship_web.py) that talks to it over WebSocket.

99_dewy_frontend.note: Dewy's own lexer and Pratt parser (ported from compiler/dewy_fast.jo) as Dewy modules: token and syntax-tree dumps for a 53-entry corpus, with the frontend's diagnostics at line:column. Also runs as wasm.

100_rtos_kernel.note: RTOS kernel (tier-4 flagship) in $no_hidden_costs modules with & no allocates & no blocks entry points and no runtime checks: fixed TCBs, priority scheduling with FIFO turns and time slices, mutexes with transitive priority inheritance, bounded mailboxes with blocked senders/receivers, a hashed timer wheel, a LIFO block pool, a bump arena and maskable latched interrupt lines, driven by a stdin event script. Hosted simulation; the bare-metal image (a $target, extern timer and device pointers) is held on question 24.

101_ml_training.note: ML training loop (tier-4 flagship): a 2-12-12-3 ReLU perceptron trained with Adam on a seeded three-class XOR cloud, per-sample backpropagation in parallel with a fixed-order gradient reduction, per-epoch loss/accuracy, held-out confusion matrix and probes, matched bit for bit (printed) by an independent float oracle. core.dewy is the twin over arrays and parallel.

102_trip_splitter.note: Split shared trip costs: functions giving several values (:>(int int)), substitution invariance (show(pair), show(saved(total)), show([d c]...)), [a b] and (a b) unpacking, record fields renamed with `as`, [first ...middle last], [head ...], swaps and record parameter patterns.

103_garden_physics.note: Garden and kitchen physics with juxtaposed products (n(n+1)/2, (l+2w)(b+2w), 4(n+1), slope(run), k(x)^2/2, 3x^2, 4spring_energy(...)) on exact quantities, int quantities promoting to rational parameters, temperature points versus differences decided by use (mean[loop ...], setpoint +/- band, boil - 5°C).

104_exact_kitchen.note: Recipe scaling, bill splitting, savings, harmonic sums and dice odds in exact rationals printed as written (fractions, decimals, repeating decimals, decimals through quantities), loop-carried products annotated rational/float64 so no growth warning fires.

105_hash_toolkit.note: FNV-1a and xorshift64* with overflow='wrap', a counting Bloom filter with overflow='saturate', Adler-32 with proven narrowing stores, and exact intermediates: uint64 midpoints, a*b % m on uint64, int64 squares over 2^63, averaged uint8 pixels.

106_login_vault.note: Credential service over a stdin script: passwords, PINs and session tokens as secret<T> (declared fields and results, secret(x), x as secret<T>); records, errors, dictionaries with secret keys and arrays print <redacted>; =? gives bool, + stays secret; .reveal feeds an audit digest.

107_static_files.note: Static file server over a request script: p"{root}/{name}" confined with root.confine(p) or_throw or guarded with root.contains(p) before any file operation, SafePath parameters, directory indexes and listings, 404/403/405, and traversal attempts (.., css/../..) refused.

108_bank_ledger.note: Mutex<int64> accounts: four teller tasks move money with lock_all (DuplicateLock for self-transfers, Overdrawn as a value), a three-lock split payment, a parallel 1% interest pass locking one account per iteration, try_lock reporting Busy, totals conserved and deterministic on two cores.

109_log_pipeline.note: Access-log report: reader -> parser -> classifier -> aggregator through the pipeline(window seeds work feedback) protocol (uncertified until a library gate proves it, so no $no_deadlocks), parser and classifier composed into its stage task, a window of 4 for backpressure, optional results counted as malformed.

110_config_loader.note: Config from stdin: `??` defaults any failure, `??<NotAnInteger>` defaults only that kind while TooManyDigits reaches a match, to_int(max_digits=) failure kinds explained, literal regexes checked while compiling as Regex, and a user-supplied pattern through regex(p) giving Regex | RegexError.

111_build_aware.note: Notes indexer adapting to its build: $target.os paths, line endings and artifact names, $target.arch word size (value ifs on $target), $build.mode self-checks and footers with only the live arm compiled, $supported_targets. expected.out is the ladder's --release build on x86_64-linux.

112_bulletproof_sensor.note: Sensor-log summarizer under $bulletproof: fixed arrays, refined Reading and Log fields, rows on every function, OutOfMemory handled, every index, division, narrowing and loop bound proven, bad lines as values.

113_bounded_log_shipper.note: A producer task ships 96 service events through a bounded four-slot channel; the consumer drains through close and tallies accepted payloads.

114_atomic_audio_meter.note: An 84-frame audio mixer writes an eight-frame ring and publishes peak and count in CachePadded<Atomic<int64>> handles.

115_libc_lengths.note: A libc strlen binding with ptr<uint8> checks 104 NUL-terminated buffers.

116_float_policy_lab.note: A finite-float guarded ratio and fast-math transform summarize 91 sensor readings under default no-traps policy.

117_csv_invoice_unpack.note: An invoice CSV batch uses record unpacking, nested/rest unpacking and a swap while reconciling 89 orders.

118_live_route_worklist.note: A live worklist traverses 85 directed route edges and a bound tree iterator skips a closed subtree.

119_binary_frame_decoder.note: A decoder reads little-endian uint64 words at proven offsets and reduces 102 bytes with wrapping uint8 conversion.

120_arena_budget_ledger.note: A ledger acquires an Arena under explicit allocation failure and books 107 entries with OutOfMemory handled as a value.

121_catalog_warnings.note: A catalog quote exercises $warn_if as a soft quantity contract and members(Tier) as an array value.

122_non_send_telemetry.note: A local-only telemetry record processes 92 readings locally and must be rejected when moved into spawn.

131_ffi_sorted_records.note: libc qsort and bsearch over C-layout records call exported Dewy comparators.

132_packet_checksum.note: IPv4/UDP datagrams built and parsed with a refined header length and a wrapping checksum.

133_concurrent_job_router.note: Bounded workers use source-qualified and conditional select waits, ticker, merged inboxes, races and reserve permits.

134_command_formatter.note: CLI inventory formatting combines rest parameters, keyword-only options, spreads, named type members, format patterns and a proven exit code.

135_ffi_image_tool.note: A compiled C image library passes and returns small and large structs by value, uses layout queries for buffers and writes nullable pointer out-parameters.

136_team_calendar.note: Team meeting planner over stdin across the 2026 daylight-saving changes: zones read at run time, local working hours as Range<Instant> intersections minus busy blocks, function-scoped $time.zone office reports reading the same pins differently, $time.fold/$time.gap settings for handoffs in a repeated and a skipped hour, weekly zoned standups and clamped monthly periods; zoneinfo oracle.

137_snapshot_backup.note: Incremental content-addressed backup over a stdin edit script: workspace, restore and manifest paths confined before any file operation, SafePath record fields and arrays (confine ?? continue), previous manifest and current scan loaded together in parallel ( ... ), FNV hashing in [parallel ...] under a function-scoped $program.max_cores, Ctrl-C listened for beside the work in the same parallel block (closes when the backup returns), and a lease released by an assigned $__drop__.

138_crate_puzzle.note: Crate-pushing puzzle replaying stdin moves on built-in 7x5 and 9x6 levels: one generic Game<W H> specialized by named integer constants, shaped [H W] grids whose integer type parameters forward between generic functions, every grid index proven by guards, unscoped ( ... ) match arms declaring the step for use after the match, and undo by keeping whole copied states.

139_staged_release.open: D40 Q2 (cleanup at block end or after last use) and Q6 (a visible exit where a local cleanup can fail); also needs self-closing files (open(path 'w')) and a fallible assigned $__abandon__ (D40 Q1/Q4, decided, not built).
139_staged_release.note: Atomic site releases: files staged through self-closing handles under a Staged owner whose assigned $__abandon__ removes the staged directory unless commit consumes it; a refused release leaves nothing behind and its cleanup failure would be the function's result.

140_word_tally.note: Command-line word tally: name=value, --flag and -f options with -- ending them, files read as text with a missing one reported on stderr and skipped, wc-style counts, words counted with counts[w] = (counts.get(w) ?? 0) + 1, the most frequent words with alphabetical ties, and a tab-separated report written to out= and read back.

141_calc_interpreter.note: Line calculator over stdin: a lexer with columns, a precedence-climbing parser building a recursive Expr union, a tree-walking evaluator over exact int and bool values with let globals, recursive user functions, if/then/else and built-ins, and every lexing, parsing and run-time mistake returned as a CalcError value with its column.

142_clinic_simulation.note: Replicated discrete-event clinic days through bounded channels: a producer and three workers over two-slot channels, splitmix64 streams, exponential arrivals and visits, urgent-first lines, a bounded waiting room, a time-ordered Heap of events carrying patients by value, a local mean closure inside spawned work, job numbers written through loop i in 0.. and @job in plan, and job-ordered per-scenario means, spreads and nearest-rank percentiles.

143_fifo_inventory.note: Post purchases, sales and damage at exact cent prices, consume FIFO lots across receipt boundaries, and reconcile margins and remaining inventory after rejected orders.

144_classifier_report.note: Report weighted confusion matrices in command-line label order, including repeated observations, abstentions, undefined class scores, stable ties and batches with no reviews.

145_log_rotation.note: Preview and perform dated log rotation in a confined spool, preserve active data on same-day collisions, and reopen the surviving logs after calendar-day expiry across leap day.

146_sensor_stream.note: Streaming sensor report over stdin through a generator pipeline (rows -> one sensor -> fixed windows with gap fill -> moving average -> hysteresis alarms): bad rows yielded as values, a deferred pull count that runs at an early stop and at the end, a combined header taking the first windows, exact rational averages and refined generator parameters.

147_timetable_solver.note: School timetable search over stdin terms: per-course period and room choices from capacity, lab and absence constraints, teacher and shared-student clashes as a nested comprehension, most-constrained-first backtracking with forward checking on value copies of the remaining choices (no undo log), record dictionary keys for the printed grid, and an infeasible term and an unplaceable course reported with the assignments tried.

148_follow_graph.note: Follow-graph report over stdin: edges parsed by a generator that yields malformed lines as values, compressed sparse rows whose targets carry a sibling-length bound so runs read through clamped slices index without checks, in-degree ranking, mutual follows, Kosaraju groups and breadth-first reach (explicit index stacks whose elements are bounded by the people count), a recursive follow tree through generator delegation, and suggestions from one row of A*A.

149_tree_diff.note: Tree diff CLI through the argparse library (positional paths, a refined `-U=` context, flags): files matched by their path below each root, a unified diff per changed text file from a longest-common-subsequence table built as `fill(fill(0 m) n)`, whitespace-insensitive keys, the no-newline marker, one-sided and binary files named, and a per-file insertion/deletion summary; the oracle re-applies every hunk.

150_build_planner.note: Build planner over stdin targets with dependencies and Duration times read by `Duration(text)`: malformed, mistimed and repeated lines reported, a recursive depth-first walk with a by-value path and an `@` state that names missing dependencies, cycles and what they block, Kahn's order with alphabetical ties, the critical path, list scheduling on N workers by longest remaining chain, and the rebuild set of each changed target.

151_ring_traffic.note: Nagel-Schreckenberg ring-road traffic CLI through argparse (refined counts and percent, a `uint64` seed, an optional light cell, a flag): an `array<Car?>` road updated in parallel each step, floored-modulo ring indexing, a seeded xorshift64* for dawdling, a red light that walls a cell on a cycle, a space-time diagram, exact mean speed formatted, cars past the light and the longest stopped queue.

152_sheet_recalc.note: Spreadsheet recalculation over stdin cells: a lexer and precedence parser for formulas with cell ranges and functions, exact fractions with guarded division, error values (#DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #ARGS!, #CYCLE!) stored in a `rational | string | Fault` cell union and spread through or_throw while `??<none>` keeps them, Kahn's order over record-keyed dictionaries with circular cells left over, a column-aligned grid, and edits from the command line that recalculate only the cells they reach.

153_ignore_rules.note: Ignore rules as a version-control tool reads them: a .gitignore-syntax file compiled into a `Literal | AnyOne | Star | Globstar | Class` piece union (escapes, bracket classes with ranges and `!`, `**` across directories, anchoring, directory-only rules, negation), unreadable patterns reported, each stdin path matched by a dynamic-programming table over its graphemes (`?` takes `é` whole) with directories deciding first, the last matching rule winning, and rules that decide nothing listed.
